job.style: a rule explained with two contrasting examples

passage: In geometry, understanding circle properties requires precision. First, consider a line drawn from the centre of a circle to a chord. This line only bisects the chord if it is perpendicular to it; a random line from the centre does not guarantee bisection. For example, if a line is drawn from the centre to a chord but is not perpendicular, the chord segments remain unequal. Second, consider tangents drawn from an external point. Two tangents drawn from any single point outside a circle are always equal in length, regardless of the circle's radius or the point's distance. For instance, if you draw two tangents from point P to a circle, they will be equal even if the circle is small or large. Third, remember that the angle in a semicircle is always 90 degrees, forming a right-angled triangle regardless of whether the triangle is isosceles or scalene. Finally, note that a cyclic quadrilateral must have its four vertices on the circle, and its opposite angles must sum to 180 degrees, not be equal to each other. A rectangle is a cyclic quadrilateral, but a random rhombus is not, as its vertices do not necessarily lie on a single circle.

items.evidence: This line only bisects the chord if it is perpendicular to it; a random line from the centre does not guarantee bisection.
items.q: A line from a circle's centre meets a chord at a slant. What happens to the chord?
options: It is cut into two equal parts
items.explain: Only a perpendicular line from the centre bisects the chord; a slanting one leaves the parts unequal.

wrong.why: thinks any line from the centre bisects the chord
thinks a chord near the centre becomes the longest
mixes up a chord with a diameter

items.evidence: Two tangents drawn from any single point outside a circle are always equal in length, regardless of the circle's radius or the point's distance.
items.q: Point P is far outside a very small circle. How do its two tangent lengths compare?
options: They are equal only if P is close
They are equal only for a large circle
items.explain: Two tangents from an outside point are always equal, whatever the circle's size or the point's distance.

wrong.why: thinks the two tangents can differ in length
thinks equality needs a special distance for P
thinks circle size changes the rule

items.evidence: Third, remember that the angle in a semicircle is always 90 degrees, forming a right-angled triangle regardless of whether the triangle is isosceles or scalene.
items.q: Why is angle ACB 90 degrees when AB is a diameter and C lies on the circle?
options: Any angle in a semicircle is a right angle
ACB is 90 degrees only if AC equals BC
The angle at C depends on where C lies
ACB is half of the angle at the centre
items.explain: The angle in a semicircle is always 90 degrees, whether the triangle is isosceles or scalene.

wrong.why: thinks the rule needs an isosceles triangle
thinks angles change with the point chosen

items.evidence: A rectangle is a cyclic quadrilateral, but a random rhombus is not, as its vertices do not necessarily lie on a single circle.
items.q: Which shows that a four-sided figure does not always fit inside one circle?
options: A random rhombus, with vertices not on one circle
A rectangle, with all four corners on a circle
A square, with four equal angles of 90 degrees
Any quadrilateral, since its angles add to 360
items.explain: A random rhombus need not have its vertices on one circle, unlike a rectangle.

wrong.why: mixes up which shape is cyclic in the passage
assumes equal angles guarantee a circle
thinks any quadrilateral lies on one circle
